School Services Agreement
How Does it Work?
In 1962, the City of Fairfax School Board entered into a four-way School
Services Agreement (SSA) with the City of Fairfax, Fairfax County, and
Fairfax County Public Schools (FCPS).

An updated agreement was negotiated in 1978 and continues to guide
the partnership.

Under the SSA, FCPS manages and operates the city schools, hires staff,
and develops the curriculum, while the City School Board oversees the
contract, provides supplemental resources, and maintains the four city-
owned school buildings.
6
School Services Agreement
How Does it Work?
Oversight: The City School Board and Superintendent are responsible for overseeing and
managing the SSA.
Board Collaboration: Members of the City School Board engage in ongoing communication with
their County counterparts.
Leadership Collaboration: The City and County Superintendents consult on topics including
boundary changes, school closings, principal selection, citizen participation, special community
needs, non-school activities, and concerns.
City Education: City students attend city schools, but access all FCPS resources and supplemental
City resources including special education services, FCPS Academies, International Baccalaureate
(IB) programs, and programs such as Thomas Jefferson High School for Science and Technology.
Advisory Participation: The City School Board appoints citizen representatives to serve on FCPS
advisory committees.
Capital Improvements: The City is responsible for major capital improvements to its school
buildings.
Welcoming Students: The City of Fairfax schools welcome county students, enabling city schools
to provide a wide variety of academic and extracurricular opportunities.  7
